cs.t: I wasn't 16 when I discovered used rack mounted servers, but I was pretty young (21 I think?). I had a miserable job paying near-subsistance wages in 2012 (about $30,000/year, no health insurance, Dallas TX).  I needed something a bit more powerful than my laptop to do some experiments with video encoding, but I couldn't afford a "fast" computer at the time, at least not fast enough to do what I wanted.  It didn't help that I was particularly bad at saving money until I was about 25. On a whim, I went on Craigslist and just looked up different ways of phrasing "fast cheap computer", and eventually stumbled upon "server".  Upon doing so, I found that you could buy dated, but still useful rack mounted servers for basically nothing; in my case a seller was selling two rack mounted Dell servers, 16 cores each, 32GB of RAM, for about $250.  I was just barely able to swing that, so I drove over, picked it up, and more or less defined the direction of my career for the next twelve years.
cs.th: Most 16-year-olds don't have servers in their rooms
